verdict.reasoning: Decreased appetite and energy: Doctor opens with "you've mentioned that you're not having much of an appetite and energy lately"; patient agrees. Intermittent shortness of breath: patient says "like I'm feeling short of breath"; later clarifies it occurs in the lift. Palpitations: patient describes "my heart starts beating" and doctor labels this as "palpitations".

Timing and trigger: Patient says loss of appetite and feeling down/low energy "must have started when I... changed over to the new law firm" and then specifies "three months ago, three and a half months ago".

Duration and amount: Doctor asks if weight loss has been "at least six months" and patient agrees "Something like that, yeah". For amount, patient says "I would say, less than a storm [stone], something like that." Doctor reflects "So about a stone, yeah? Six months" and patient does not disagree.
Nausea: Patient says "I feel nauseous every now and again". Vomiting: When asked "Have you been ever sick with it?" patient replies "No, actually not."

Lift episodes: Patient says in the lift "my heart starts beating, I, I feel like I can't breathe"; doctor summarizes as palpitations. Exercise tolerance: Doctor states "you can walk about a mile and you don't feel short of breath at all" and patient answers "That's right, yes." Chest pain: Doctor asks "You get any chest pains with it?" and both then confirm "no chest pains" / "No chest pain."

Headaches at work: Patient says "I have trouble at work sometimes, having headaches, feeling nauseous." Low mood: Patient repeatedly describes feeling "down" and doctor clarifies "would you say you're depressed?"; patient acknowledges difficulty but overall presents low mood.

Bowels: Patient says toilet is "OK... I don't really have problems". Diarrhea: When asked "you don't have any diarrhoea?" patient replies "Uh, no. No diarrhoea." Blood/mucus: Doctor asks "there's blood in the poo no mucus nothing of that sort?" patient replies "no, no, nothing." Reflux: Doctor asks "Do you suffer from acid reflux?" patient says "I do not, no." Cough: Doctor asks "is there any cough?" patient: "Um, no, not really".
Patient states "I had too little activity of my thyroid" and doctor restates "underactive thyroid" which is hypothyroidism.
Patient says "In view of that, I took thyroxine" and later "I have not been taking it in the last, actually since I changed doctor, I would say."
Occupation: Patient jokes "who likes to be a lawyer?" confirming he is a lawyer. Marital status: Patient mentions "my, my, my wife was starting to complain" indicating he is married.

The transcript lists fatigue, loss of appetite, weight loss, and low mood, and the doctor mentions checking "anaemia" and "vitamin levels" and reviewing thyroid, but there is no explicit statement that these diagnoses must be specifically ruled out, nor any mention of depression as a differential; this causal/diagnostic framing is added clinical reasoning.

Palpitations and shortness of breath in the lift are described, but the doctor does not explicitly attribute them to anxiety or cardiovascular causes; that differential is additional interpretation not stated in the transcript.
History of hypothyroidism: patient and doctor confirm "underactive thyroid." Currently off thyroxine: patient states "I have not been taking it... since I changed doctor."

Doctor says "I think a general set of bloods is a good start... we look at things like anaemia, how your kidney functions are, your livers, all that, with vitamin levels, and your [thyroid]." This corresponds to FBC, U&E, LFT, TFT, and vitamin levels, though the abbreviations themselves are not used.

Doctor explains that after the blood tests "when you get the result, you will receive a text message through your phone to tell you to book an appointment" which implies follow-up consultation via the app after reviewing results.

Chest pain/palpitations: Doctor says "with palpitations or chest pain... that's more of a medical emergency. You need to go to A and E for that." Bowel/vomiting: Doctor says "if your, you know, bowels change or you're being sick again, you need to get in touch with us."
Doctor instructs "you need to ring up support... so that we can organise that blood test for you" and later clarifies "there's a number on your app... So just call that number."
